research_notes.logo: Cranfield's primary wordmark is only published as a white-on-transparent SVG. It is linked from the site header as //www.cranfield.ac.uk/~/media/newlogowhite.ashx and probing it returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/svg+xml (5686 bytes), but downloading it shows the only fill declared is .st0 { fill: #fff }, i.e. white artwork with no coloured or dark variant on the domain. That is banned by the brief, so I looked for the awarding body's own brand icon set, which Cranfield references in its own page markup under /~/media/brand/. I probed the set: androidicon192x192.png (200, image/png, 22004 bytes), appleicon180x180.png (200, image/png, 19882 bytes), msicon144x144.png (200, image/png, 14570 bytes) and favicon96x96.png (200, image/png, 10263 bytes) are all real images on www.cranfield.ac.uk; /favicon.ico and /apple-touch-icon.png return 404, and other guessed paths such as /~/media/brand/logo.svg return the site's HTML 404 page rather than an image. I downloaded appleicon180x180.png and inspected the pixels: 180x180, Format32bppArgb, 20187 transparent pixels and 12213 opaque pixels, all 12213 of them dark (dominant colour RGB 12,64,109, Cranfield navy) with 0 light pixels. It is therefore a dark/coloured official Cranfield mark on the awarding body's own domain, visible on a light card, and not white-on-transparent, so it is reported as the logo. I chose appleicon180x180.png because the brief explicitly names /apple-touch-icon.png as an acceptable source and it is the largest brand asset that is an actual image rather than an icon crop.
